title: The Evening Brief: Governance under test: LSU, LIV, and a Big Ten fix
dek: The SEC's Thursday expulsion vote on LSU draws closer, LIV Golf's bankruptcy details harden, and the Big Ten expands its replay-audio transparency fix as new NFL and college contracts land alongside two American tennis semifinalists.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's institutions all moved to add transparency or accountability, from LIV's bankruptcy filing to the Big Ten's replay audio expansion, while the SEC's LSU vote and the MAC's Michigan appeal test whether governing bodies can enforce or overturn decisions once made.
bottom_line: Wednesday's common thread was institutions facing tests of their own rules: the SEC moving toward a Thursday expulsion vote against LSU, LIV Golf detailing its finances in a Chapter 11 filing, the MAC appealing a disputed clock ruling to the NCAA and CFP, and the Big Ten expanding live replay audio after scrutiny of its review process. The reporting establishes what each body has filed or announced but not how any of these disputes will resolve, since court approval, conference votes, and oversight committee responses all remain pending. Alongside the institutional stories, contract news for Christian Gonzalez and Baker Mayfield and Aaron Judge's return added a separate, calmer track of the day. Watch Thursday's SEC vote, the Big Ten's September 12 replay audio launch, and Friday's Shelton-Tiafoe semifinal as the next concrete markers.
body: The throughline today is institutions being asked to account for themselves, in court, in a vote, or on live broadcast. The SEC's amended federal complaint against LSU, filed Tuesday, escalates toward Thursday's vote of conference presidents on expulsion, an action the SEC's own filing notes has no precedent in the conference's 94-year history. LIV Golf's Chapter 11 filing in New Jersey laid out exactly how far its finances have fallen short of its obligations. And the Big Ten, following its Big Ten Replay Center criticism, announced it will broadcast live replay-review audio across all conference games starting Saturday, September 12.

On the roster and contract side, the Patriots signed cornerback Christian Gonzalez to a four-year, $135 million extension with $102 million guaranteed, making him the NFL's highest-paid cornerback at $33.75 million average annual value, edging Devon Witherspoon's Seahawks deal. The move landed less than 48 hours before New England's opener against Seattle. The Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield ended their own months-long standoff with a three-year, $165 million extension at $55 million average annual value, tying him for third among NFL quarterbacks. Aaron Judge was reinstated from the 60-day injured list Monday and was expected to play Tuesday's opener against Colorado, his first appearance since May 31 after a rib stress fracture; the Yankees were 36-23 when he last played and 45-39 without him through Sunday, ranking 26th in the majors in runs scored from June 1 onward.

In college football, the MAC filed formal appeals to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the CFP, arguing Michigan's 13-12 win over Western Michigan should be overturned because the Big Ten replay crew used the wrong clock feed to restore a second to the clock. Washington's win over Washington State in the Apple Cup came at a cost: starting running back Quaid Carr will need surgery for a hand injury and backup Jayden Limar sustained an elbow injury, with coach Jedd Fisch declining to rule out season-ending outcomes for either. And Monday's SMU-Florida State game played out without stadium lights or coach-to-player communication after a transformer failure at Doak Campbell Stadium, a nearly two-hour delay that still ended with a completed game.

Beyond football, Cricket Australia approved Big Bash League privatization with a self-determination model letting individual states choose their own path, launching a sales process for the Melbourne Renegades toward the 2027-28 season. The College Sports Commission cleared $227 million in NIL deals in July and August, nearly double its first year's total. The RFU will extend Steve Borthwick's contract past the 2028 Six Nations, with his tenure beyond the 2027 World Cup left contingent on results in Australia. And in New York, Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 in a match ending at 3:34 a.m. ET, the latest finish in US Open history, while Frances Tiafoe completed a two-set comeback over Alex Michelsen, setting up an all-American men's semifinal Friday and guaranteeing the tournament's first American finalist since 2003.

The reporting attributes today's institutional moves to specific triggers: the SEC's action follows LSU rostering players who had signed NFL contracts; LIV's bankruptcy follows the Saudi PIF ending its funding in April; the Big Ten's replay expansion follows scrutiny of its Replay Center's handling of contested calls, including the clock dispute now central to the MAC's appeal. Where the inputs do not specify a cause, such as full details behind Cricket Australia's retreat from league-wide privatization beyond stated state opposition, that is left as reported.
Desk boards were unavailable this run, so figures above come directly from the day's reporting rather than a live scoreboard cross-check.

The coming days carry several fixed checkpoints. The SEC's presidents vote on LSU expulsion is scheduled for Thursday, September 10, requiring a two-thirds majority under conference bylaws, with a separate Louisiana state court injunction complicating any enforcement. LIV Golf's BC Partners restructuring agreement still needs court and stakeholder approval, with the gap between $49.6 million in available financing and up to $1 billion in estimated liabilities still unresolved. The CFP and ESPN have until December 1 to reach a media rights agreement on 24-team expansion, the same date conferences must notify broadcast partners on conference championship game plans. The Big Ten's expanded replay audio launches Saturday, September 12. And Shelton faces Tiafoe in Friday's US Open semifinal, with the winner reaching Sunday's final against the tournament's other finalist.
